items.title: Fix FORGE linear and angular velocity observations
items.body:
### Description

FORGE's parent update overwrites pose history before the child computes noisy finite differences, causing policy velocity observations to lose actual motion.

This PR gives FORGE separate noisy position and orientation history, initializes it with the environment tensors, and synchronizes it with the final noisy observations after reset settling. Factory's true-pose history is no longer overwritten by the child.

It also corrects the XYZW quaternion projection to retain x/y, which encode yaw for the tool's roll-pi orientation. An inline comment explains why z/w are cleared.

Related to #8874.

### Changes addressing review feedback

- Added FORGE-owned noisy-pose history and explicit reset synchronization.
- Documented the upright-tool quaternion projection.
- Replaced fixed `torch.randn` return sequences with seeded real sampling.
- Checked velocities against independently recorded consecutive noisy poses.
- Added a reset-history regression to ensure a reset pose jump does not become velocity in the next stationary sample.

The tests execute production tensor initialization and update methods with lightweight backend data. The reset test supplies the parent's completed reset pose and observations without running physics settling.

### Validation

Local CPU source-method validation:

```bash
UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/forge_review_uv_cache uv run --no-project --offline \
  --python /home/feng/miniconda3/envs/isaaclab51/bin/python \
  python /tmp/forge_velocity_review_v2/run_isolated_regression.py \
  --forge-source /home/feng/fixx/IsaacLab-forge-fix/source/isaaclab_tasks/isaaclab_tasks/contrib/forge/forge_env.py \
  --test-source /home/feng/fixx/IsaacLab-forge-fix/source/isaaclab_tasks/test/contrib/test_forge_velocity.py
```

Results:

- Updated implementation: **3 passed, 0 failed**.
- Original upstream implementation: **0 passed, 3 failed**.
- Removing reset-history synchronization alone: **2 passed, 1 failed**.
- Adding an unrelated random draw: **3 passed, 0 failed**, confirming that the tests do not depend on a fixed sampling-call count.

This temporary local harness loads the complete production initialization, update, and FORGE reset methods plus production math utilities, bypassing backend/configuration imports. It is not included in the PR and does not constitute normal pytest or simulator validation.

The committed tests use normal imports. In a configured Isaac Lab 3.0 environment, run:

```bash
uv run python -m pytest source/isaaclab_tasks/test/contrib/test_forge_velocity.py
```

Normal pytest collection was blocked locally by missing `isaaclab_physx` in the existing Python 3.11 environment.

Repository-wide formatting, lint, and changelog hooks passed except the Git LFS pointer hook, which could not run because `git-lfs` is not installed. `git diff --check` also passed.

Full simulator validation has not been performed.

### Compatibility

The changelog notes that policy velocity inputs change and existing checkpoints may need retraining. No training or sim-to-real performance improvement is claimed.

items.title: [Bug Report] FORGE policy linear velocity loses motion due to overwritten position history
items.body:
### Describe the bug

In `ForgeEnv`, the policy's `ee_linvel` observation appears to lose the actual end-effector motion because `FactoryEnv` and `ForgeEnv` reuse and update the same position-history buffer during one call.

Checked on October 29, 2026 against **v3.0.0** (`e3f7d9ff1f5d7f8280de3ece9000b7117f66bcf4`), the latest stable release at the time of checking, and **main at `0ca25c56eec6fe7860fdcba44f8848f19693d6f6`**. Both contain the same linear-velocity bookkeeping. The issue is also present in v2.3.0.

**I would be happy to work on a fix and submit a PR with regression tests. Before implementing it, I would appreciate confirmation of the intended observation semantics and the preferred fix direction, as described below.**

1. `ForgeEnv._compute_intermediate_values(dt)` first calls `super()._compute_intermediate_values(dt)`.
2. The parent computes a finite-difference velocity, then immediately replaces `self.prev_fingertip_pos` with the **current true position**.
3. The child computes a noisy position and overwrites `self.ee_linvel_fd` using that already-updated buffer.

Consequently, with `p_t` the current true position and `epsilon_t` its additive observation noise:

```text
actual ee_linvel_fd = ((p_t + epsilon_t) - p_t) / dt
                   = epsilon_t / dt
```

The result is independent of the actual displacement. Disabling position noise makes the observed linear velocity zero even while the end effector moves.

If the intent is finite differencing noisy position measurements, the expected result is:

```text
expected ee_linvel_fd = ((p_t + epsilon_t) - (p_previous + epsilon_previous)) / dt
```

Here `previous` means the previous position sample at the interval represented by `dt`, which need not be the previous policy decision.

### Source references

Permalinks to the checked main commit:

- [Parent updates position history: factory_env.py, lines 115–116](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/0ca25c56eec6fe7860fdcba44f8848f19693d6f6/source/isaaclab_tasks/isaaclab_tasks/contrib/factory/factory_env.py#L115-L116).
- [Child calls parent, adds noise, and overwrites velocity: forge_env.py, lines 66–91](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/0ca25c56eec6fe7860fdcba44f8848f19693d6f6/source/isaaclab_tasks/isaaclab_tasks/contrib/forge/forge_env.py#L66-L91).
- [Policy uses ee_linvel_fd; critic uses simulator velocity: factory_env.py, lines 133–153](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/0ca25c56eec6fe7860fdcba44f8848f19693d6f6/source/isaaclab_tasks/isaaclab_tasks/contrib/factory/factory_env.py#L133-L153).

`ForgeEnv._get_observations()` retains this `ee_linvel` entry when constructing the policy observation, and the default `ForgeEnvCfg.obs_order` includes it. Thus this affects the actor's linear-velocity input. The critic's linear-velocity entry uses a different variable.

### Steps to reproduce

The following reduced reproducer preserves the original velocity statements and parent/child call order, while supplying positions directly. It requires only Python and PyTorch; it does **not** launch Isaac Sim.

```python
import torch


class FactoryEnv:
    def _compute_intermediate_values(self, dt):
        self.ee_linvel_fd = (self.fingertip_midpoint_pos - self.prev_fingertip_pos) / dt
        self.prev_fingertip_pos = self.fingertip_midpoint_pos.clone()


class ForgeEnv(FactoryEnv):
    def _compute_intermediate_values(self, dt):
        super()._compute_intermediate_values(dt)
        self.ee_linvel_fd = (self.noisy_fingertip_pos - self.prev_fingertip_pos) / dt
        self.prev_fingertip_pos = self.noisy_fingertip_pos.clone()


dt = 0.01
env = ForgeEnv()
env.prev_fingertip_pos = torch.zeros((1, 3), dtype=torch.float64)

for step in range(1, 6):
    # Move 10 mm per update; disable position noise.
    env.fingertip_midpoint_pos = torch.tensor([[step * 0.01, 0, 0]], dtype=torch.float64)
    env.noisy_fingertip_pos = env.fingertip_midpoint_pos.clone()
    env._compute_intermediate_values(dt)
    print(f"step {step}: expected vx=1.0 m/s, actual vx={env.ee_linvel_fd[0, 0].item():.1f} m/s")
    assert torch.count_nonzero(env.ee_linvel_fd).item() == 0
```

Actual output on all five updates: `actual vx=0.0 m/s`; expected: `1.0 m/s`. This demonstrates that the issue persists beyond the initial update.

With a previous noise of zero and a current x-position noise of `0.00025 m`, the same `0.01 m` displacement and `0.01 s` interval give `0.025 m/s` instead of the expected noisy finite difference of `1.025 m/s`.

### System Info

- Source versions: v3.0.0 and main commit listed above.
- Reproducer: CPU tensors, PyTorch 2.7.0+cu128.
- Isaac Sim / GPU / driver: not used by this reduced reproducer. A full simulator rollout on the latest release has not been performed.

### Additional context

This report establishes the history-buffer overwrite and its connection to policy observations. It does not establish the magnitude of any training or sim-to-real performance impact.

### Proposed fix and questions for maintainers

The comment "Repeat finite differencing with noisy fingertip positions" suggests that the intended observation is the difference between consecutive noisy position samples divided by their sampling interval.

My proposed approach is to give FORGE a dedicated previous-noisy-position buffer, keeping the parent's true-position history separate. The buffer would be initialized/reset for the affected environment IDs and updated once per position sample. This should preserve Factory's history while allowing FORGE to compute the noisy finite difference.

Before I implement the fix, could you please confirm:

1. **Expected behavior:** Should the actor's `ee_linvel` be the finite difference of consecutive noisy position measurements, as in the expected formula above, or is a different velocity observation intended?
2. **Fix direction:** Would a separate noisy-position history buffer in FORGE be appropriate, or would you prefer a change to the parent/child update structure?
3. **Reset and compatibility:** Should the velocity observation be zeroed on reset, with noisy history initialized from the reset sample? Are there existing-checkpoint compatibility requirements the PR should follow?

If this approach is appropriate and nobody is already working on it, I would be happy to prepare a focused PR covering zero-noise motion, noisy consecutive samples, and reset behavior, following the project's testing conventions.

The angular-velocity path also reuses a history buffer updated by the parent. I would keep this report's verified finding focused on linear velocity and ask whether you would like the analogous angular-history behavior investigated in the same PR or separately.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched the repository's open/closed issues and PRs for FORGE and relevant variable names and did not find a matching report.
- [x] The reduced reproducer isolates repository-level tensor bookkeeping without running Isaac Sim.

### Proposed Acceptance Criteria (pending confirmation of intended behavior)

- [ ] With position noise disabled, nonzero displacement over a known sampling interval produces the expected nonzero policy linear velocity.
- [ ] With noise enabled, the result includes the true displacement and the difference between consecutive position-noise samples.
- [ ] History is handled consistently across resets and repeated updates, with appropriate regression coverage.

items.title: Support Python 3.14 annotations in `configclass`
items.body:
# Description

On Python 3.14, any `@configclass` without `from __future__ import annotations` fails at class creation:

```text
ValueError: The number of annotations (0) does not match the number of class members (3).
```

Python 3.14 evaluates annotations lazily ([PEP 649](https://peps.python.org/pep-0649/)), and they are no longer stored in `cls.__dict__["__annotations__"]`, which is where `configclass` reads the annotations declared in a class body. I hit it with `RigidBodyFragment` while packaging Isaac Lab for conda-forge (conda-forge/staged-recipes#34602): the package is `noarch: python`, so the environments that run the `isaaclab` CLI there resolve Python 3.14.

This PR adds a small `_own_annotations(cls)` helper that uses `annotationlib.get_annotations(cls, format=Format.FORWARDREF)` on 3.14 and keeps the class dictionary lookup on older versions. `FORWARDREF` leaves forward references unresolved, matching the pre-3.14 behavior. The three places that read `__dict__["__annotations__"]` now go through the helper.

`test_functions_config` read `cfg.__annotations__` from an instance, which 3.14 no longer exposes, so it now reads them from `type(cfg)`.

The root `pyproject.toml` still declares `requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"`. This change does not widen it, it only removes a blocker for installs that end up on 3.14 anyway, like the conda-forge one.

items.title: Drop Kit's bundled Python stdlib from PYTHONPATH in isaaclab.sh
items.body:
# Description

With a pre-built Isaac Sim 6.0 binary linked as `_isaac_sim` and a conda environment from `./isaaclab.sh --conda`, `./isaaclab.sh --install` fails on its first step (`pip install --upgrade pip`) with:

```
  File ".../_isaac_sim/kit/python/lib/python3.12/platform.py", line 1110, in _sys_version
ValueError: failed to parse CPython sys.version: '3.12.14 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Aug 21 2026, 22:48:28) [GCC 14.4.0]'
```

Isaac Sim 6.0 ships no `setup_conda_env.sh`, so `isaaclab.sh` sources `setup_python_env.sh`, which appends Kit's **entire bundled Python stdlib** (`kit/python/lib/python3.12`) to `PYTHONPATH`. `PYTHONPATH` entries precede the interpreter's own stdlib on `sys.path`, so the bundled `platform.py` shadows the conda one. Its older `sys_version_parser` regex has no handling for the conda-forge `"| packaged by conda-forge |"` version string, so `platform.python_version()` raises — and pip calls it to build its user agent, so every pip invocation in the env fails.

The existing workaround in `isaaclab.sh` (prepending the env's `site-packages`) does not help here, because a stdlib directory rather than a package is being shadowed.

This PR filters that single directory out of `PYTHONPATH` right after sourcing `setup_python_env.sh`. Kit's `site-packages`, `python_packages`, extension and `pip_prebundle` paths are untouched.

Verified with Isaac Sim `6.0.0-rc.59` binary + conda-forge Python 3.12.14: `--install` completes, `scripts/tutorials/00_sim/create_empty.py` runs, and `scripts/reinforcement_learning/train.py --rl_library rsl_rl --task Isaac-Cartpole` trains.

Note: the same issue could alternatively be fixed on the Isaac Sim side by not adding the stdlib directory in `setup_python_env.sh`; this change makes Isaac Lab work with the already-shipped 6.0 binaries regardless.

Fixes #7417

items.title: Clamp OSC impedance parameters without writing through the command
items.body:
# Description

`OperationalSpaceController.set_command` clamps the impedance parameters it resolves from `command` in place. `torch.split` returns views that alias `command`, so in the `variable` and `variable_kp` impedance modes the clamp writes through those views into the caller's tensor. Three caller patterns that the API permits fail:

- a command shared by all environments (`command.expand(num_envs, -1)`) raises `RuntimeError: unsupported operation: more than one element of the written-to tensor refers to a single memory location. Please clone() the tensor before performing the operation.`
- a command that carries a gradient raises `RuntimeError: Output 1 of SplitWithSizesBackward0 is a view and is being modified inplace. ...`
- otherwise the caller's buffer is silently rewritten: with the default limits a stiffness of 2000 comes back as 1000 and -5 as 0, and a damping ratio of 200 as 100.

The docstring documents `command` as an input of shape `(num_envs, action_dim)` and documents no mutation; `DifferentialIKController.set_command` and the `fixed` impedance mode do not write to their input either.

The clamp now produces new tensors, so the caller's command is neither written to nor required to be writable. The resulting gains are unchanged: they match the in-place clamp for in-range, out-of-range and boundary values.

Fixes # (no issue — the defect was not reported)

## Type of change

- Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Validation

`source/isaaclab/test/controllers/test_operational_space_unit.py` is new and marked `pytest.mark.unit`, so it runs without launching the simulator:

```
pytest source/isaaclab/test/controllers/test_operational_space_unit.py
with the change: 6 passed
```

Three cases cover the caller-visible behaviour: an expanded command, a `requires_grad` command, and a writable command that must come back unchanged, for both impedance modes that split the command. The fourth asserts the clamped gains themselves (above the upper limit, below a non-zero lower limit, exactly on both boundaries, and in range, including the derived damping gains), so deleting the clamps fails the suite instead of passing it. Against the unmodified controller the first cases raise; with the clamps removed and the rest of the change kept, the gain case fails for both modes. `isaaclab --format` over the changed files passes.

The clamp now allocates one or two `(num_envs, 6)` tensors per call instead of writing in place. On CPU (`torch 2.11.0`, Ryzen 7 7840H, 4096 environments), `torch.clamp` takes 2.7 us against 1.9 us for `clip_`, so `set_command` gains about 0.8 us and 96 KB against a 4.3-4.6 ms call: under 0.1 %, and the call is dominated by the task-to-root frame rotation.

Not run: `source/isaaclab/test/controllers/test_operational_space.py`, which launches the simulator, and the full suite. The only in-tree training path, `OperationalSpaceControllerAction.process_actions`, clamps to the same limits before calling `set_command`, so training is unaffected; `scripts/tutorials/05_controllers/run_osc.py` calls `set_command` directly but with gains inside the limits. The crashes and the mutation affect direct callers of the public API.

items.title: [Bug Report] FORGE roll clipping can move away from the upright target after Euler API migration
items.body:
### Describe the bug

FORGE can command roll motion away from the upright target near the +/-180-degree boundary.

In `ForgeEnv._apply_action()`, the current and desired orientations are converted using `euler_xyz_from_quat()` without `wrap_to_2pi=True`. The subsequent clipping code maps negative desired roll into a positive range, but leaves current roll in the signed range.

For example, a physical roll of 181 degrees is returned as -179 degrees. With a target of 180 degrees, the code computes an error of +359 degrees instead of -1 degree. After clipping, this can command motion away from the target.

Source inspection on October 21, 2026 confirmed the affected code in official v3.0.0, commit `e3f7d9ff1f5d7f8280de3ece9000b7117f66bcf4`.

Relevant source:
- [FORGE action processing](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/v3.0.0/source/isaaclab_tasks/isaaclab_tasks/contrib/forge/forge_env.py#L205)
- [Euler conversion](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/v3.0.0/source/isaaclab/isaaclab/utils/math.py#L431)

### Steps to reproduce

The following dependency-free scalar example illustrates the roll conversion and subtraction for a pure X-axis rotation. It is a numerical illustration of the calculation, not a full FORGE environment or PyTorch regression test.

Save as `reproduce_roll.py` and run:

```bash
python reproduce_roll.py
```

```python
import math

target = math.pi
cap = math.radians(5.0)  # Illustrative cap, not a training configuration.

for physical_roll in (181.0, 200.0):
    angle = math.radians(physical_roll)
    current = math.atan2(math.sin(angle), math.cos(angle))

    delta = target - current
    wrapped_delta = target - (current % (2.0 * math.pi))

    step = max(-cap, min(delta, cap))
    wrapped_step = max(-cap, min(wrapped_delta, cap))

    print(
        f"current={physical_roll:.0f}, target=180, "
        f"unwrapped_next={physical_roll + math.degrees(step):.0f}, "
        f"wrapped_next={physical_roll + math.degrees(wrapped_step):.0f}"
    )
```

Output:

```text
current=181, target=180, unwrapped_next=186, wrapped_next=180
current=200, target=180, unwrapped_next=205, wrapped_next=195
```

Expected behavior:
The clipped roll command should move toward 180 degrees while respecting the per-step motion limit.

Actual behavior in this calculation:
The signed current roll and positive desired roll produce a step in the opposite direction.

### System Info

Source inspected:
- Isaac Lab: official v3.0.0.
- Commit: `e3f7d9ff1f5d7f8280de3ece9000b7117f66bcf4`.
- Validation: source inspection and scalar math; no simulator or GPU is required for the example above.

Earlier affected training setup:
- Isaac Lab: 3.0.0 beta2.
- Isaac Sim Version: 6.0.1.0.
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (AutoDL).

The original AutoDL instance was cloned to another RTX 5090 host after the original GPU became unavailable.

The following details were collected from the cloned instance on October 22, 2026:
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS.
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090.
- CUDA: 12.8 (PyTorch CUDA build).
- GPU Driver: 580.76.05.

The original host's GPU driver version was not recorded. The driver version above describes the current host.

I have not rerun training on official v3.0.0. The earlier beta2 training setup and the current cloned instance should not be interpreted as an end-to-end runtime test of official v3.0.0.

### Additional context

A candidate correction is to explicitly request the angle range expected by the existing controller at both orientation conversions in `_apply_action()`:

```python
curr_roll, curr_pitch, curr_yaw = euler_xyz_from_quat(
    self.fingertip_midpoint_quat, wrap_to_2pi=True
)
desired_roll, desired_pitch, desired_yaw = euler_xyz_from_quat(
    ctrl_target_fingertip_preclipped_quat, wrap_to_2pi=True
)
```

This would preserve the existing controller's angle-range assumptions without changing the shared math utility's default.

I would like to contribute a focused fix and a regression test that exercises the actual FORGE control path. The proposed correction should also be checked against the task's yaw joint-limit convention.

Please let me know if this issue is already tracked or if a different correction is preferred.

### Checklist

- [x] I have checked that there is no similar issue in the repo (**required**)
- [x] I have checked that the issue is not in running Isaac Sim itself and is related to the repo

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Roll commands near the +/-180-degree boundary move toward the upright target and obey the per-step motion limit.
- [ ] A regression test exercises the actual FORGE control path, fails before the fix, and passes after it.
- [ ] The task's yaw joint-limit behavior remains covered and correct.

items.title: Fix FORGE wrench transforms and PhysX joint-wrench frames
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #3513 and the PhysX joint-wrench frame discrepancy discussed in #7978.

`forge_utils.change_FT_frame` used the inverse rotation and the wrong lever-arm sign when expressing a wrench in another frame. It now computes the source pose in the target frame and applies:

- `f_t = R_ts f_s`
- `tau_t = R_ts tau_s + p_ts × f_t`

The existing independent point-force test covers translated frames with identity and arbitrary rotations. FORGE's current force-only observation remains unchanged because its call uses identity rotations.

The PhysX sensor had a separate error: `get_link_incoming_joint_force()` already returns forces and torques in the child-side joint frame, about its anchor. The sensor applied `localPos1` and `localRot1` again. It now exposes the native components directly, removing the redundant USD traversal, frame buffers, and GPU transformations. This follows the [PhysX tensor API contract](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/kit/docs/omni_physics/108.0/extensions/runtime/source/omni.physics.tensors/docs/api/python.html#omni.physics.tensors.impl.api.ArticulationView.get_link_incoming_joint_force).

Replaced the circular PhysX frame test with one shared integration fixture used by both Newton and PhysX. It uses the same timestep, geometry, loads, expected values, and tolerances: a passive vertical hinge supports a 2 kg body through an offset child frame rotated 90 degrees relative to the body. The articulation is also rotated about world Z. Both backends must report `F=(0, 0, 19.62) N` and `tau=(-1.962, 4.905, 0) N·m`, calculated from gravity and the known lever arm. The test checks that the body stays at rest. No raw wrench or production conversion is used to calculate the reference.

The fixture reuses the existing simple articulation asset with temporary USD overrides; no asset is added to the repository. The existing backend test files invoke the shared check. Removed the old circular reference helper.

## Validation

- Newton sensor suite and FORGE tests: 12 passed.
- PhysX sensor suite: 16 passed, including eager/recorded updates and reset behavior.
- The shared physical test failed with the original PhysX implementation, with a 19.62 N force-component error, and passed after removing the duplicate transform. Newton passes the same analytic contract.
- Architecture audit and `uv run --no-sync isaaclab -f` passed.
- Recorded GPU update microbenchmark at 1024 environments × 8 links: approximately 3 microseconds per launch before and after. Initialization no longer scans USD joint frames or allocates their buffers.

items.title: [Bug Report] ./isaaclab.sh --install fails with Isaac Sim 6.0 binaries + conda: "failed to parse CPython sys.version"
items.body:
### Describe the bug

With a pre-built Isaac Sim 6.0 binary linked as `_isaac_sim` and a conda environment created by `./isaaclab.sh --conda`, `./isaaclab.sh --install` fails on its very first step (`pip install --upgrade pip`):

```
  File "/home/<user>/IsaacLab/_isaac_sim/kit/python/lib/python3.12/platform.py", line 1160, in python_version
  File "/home/<user>/IsaacLab/_isaac_sim/kit/python/lib/python3.12/platform.py", line 1110, in _sys_version
ValueError: failed to parse CPython sys.version: '3.12.14 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Aug 21 2026, 22:48:28) [GCC 14.4.0]'
[ERROR] Command failed with code 2: ".../envs/env_isaaclab/bin/python -m pip install --upgrade pip"
```

Note the traceback: the conda interpreter is importing `platform.py` from **Isaac Sim's bundled stdlib**, not its own.

### Root cause

Isaac Sim 6.0 ships no `setup_conda_env.sh`, so `isaaclab.sh` falls back to sourcing `_isaac_sim/setup_python_env.sh`. That script appends `kit/python/lib/python3.12` (the entire stdlib of the bundled interpreter) to `PYTHONPATH`. `PYTHONPATH` entries precede the interpreter's own stdlib on `sys.path`, so every stdlib module that differs between the two builds is shadowed.

The bundled `platform.py` has an older `sys_version_parser` regex without the `(?:\|[^|]*\|)?` group that CPython added for the conda-forge `"| packaged by conda-forge |"` version string, so `platform.python_version()` raises. pip calls it when building its user agent, so *every* pip invocation in the env fails.

`isaaclab.sh` already prepends the env's `site-packages` to work around the `pip_prebundle` shadowing, but that does not help here because the stdlib directory is being shadowed, not a package.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Isaac Sim 6.0.0 binary (tested: `6.0.0-rc.59+release.41464.5f2772bc.glapps`) at `/opt/isaacsim`.
2. `git clone -b release/3.0.0 https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab.git && cd IsaacLab && ln -s /opt/isaacsim _isaac_sim`
3. `./isaaclab.sh --conda env_isaaclab && conda activate env_isaaclab` (creates Python 3.12.14 from conda-forge)
4. `./isaaclab.sh --install` → fails as above.

Same code path exists on `develop`.

### System Info

- Commit: `release/3.0.0` @ 2799120 (`develop` has identical `isaaclab.sh`)
- Isaac Sim: 6.0.0-rc.59 (binary)
- OS: Ubuntu, kernel 7.0
- GPU: RTX 4070 Laptop, driver 595.84
- Python (conda-forge): 3.12.14

items.title: [Proposal] Newton JointWrenchSensor: report in-tree FIXED joints (wrist F/T parity with PhysX)
items.body:
### Problem

On the Newton backend, `JointWrenchSensor` excludes every `JointType.FIXED` joint (`isaaclab_newton/sensors/joint_wrench/joint_wrench_sensor.py`, `exclude_joint_types=[JointType.FREE, JointType.FIXED]`; also documented in `docs/source/concepts/sensors/joint_wrench_sensor.rst`). Bodies attached through a weld therefore never appear in `body_names`.

That covers wrist F/T mounts and tool flanges, e.g. FR3 `fr3_joint8` / `fr3_hand_joint` and FORGE's `force_sensor` body. On PhysX every link is reported, so `SceneEntityCfg("joint_wrench", body_names=["force_sensor"])` works on PhysX but not on Newton. Discussion #7788 raises the same point.

### Evidence the data is already there

With Newton 1.6.0 (SolverMuJoCo on the Warp CPU device), I built a chain world → fixed base → revolute link (1 kg) → fixed tool (0.5 kg). At rest:
- `body_parent_f[tool]` = 4.905 N, exactly m·g.
- The existing `joint_wrench_to_incoming_joint_frame_kernel` returns the analytic joint-frame wrench: F_z = 4.905 N and τ = 0.736 N·m on the weld, F_z = 14.715 N and τ = 5.886 N·m on the revolute joint.

No new kernel is needed.

### Proposed design

Since #7295 the sensor reuses the articulation's cached view, which also excludes FIXED joints, so changing `exclude_joint_types` in the sensor alone would be a no-op. Instead:
- Keep the shared view for the body-level bindings (`body_parent_f`, `body_q`, `body_com` already cover welded links).
- Build the sensor's joint list and `joint_child` / `joint_X_c` from the model arrays (`articulation_start`/`end`, `joint_type`, `joint_parent`).
- Include FIXED joints with a non-world parent.
- Keep excluding FREE joints, world-root welds (matching PhysX's zero root) and loop-closure welds (which MuJoCo turns into WELD equalities).
- Update the docstring and `joint_wrench_sensor.rst`.
- Add a Newton regression test (hanging payload on a weld equals m·g) and a PhysX parity check.

Would you accept a PR along these lines, or would you prefer an opt-in cfg flag (e.g. `include_fixed_joints`)?

I work on contact-rich insertion on a real Franka FR3 and need the wrist F/T reading on Newton. I'm happy to implement it and validate it on H100s.

items.title: Clarifies Factory vs FORGE action-space control semantics
items.body:
# Description

The Factory and FORGE environments share the `CtrlCfg` fields `pos_action_bounds` / `rot_action_bounds` and `pos_action_threshold` / `rot_action_threshold`, but apply them in *opposite roles*, because the two families use different action spaces:

| | Factory (`factory_env.py`) | FORGE (`forge_env.py`) |
|---|---|---|
| Action meaning | displacement relative to current EE pose | absolute target relative to fixed asset |
| `pos_action_threshold` | **scales** the normalized action to a per-step displacement | **clips** the per-step motion of the target w.r.t. the current EE pose |
| `pos_action_bounds` | **clips** the target relative to the fixed asset (workspace bound) | **scales** the normalized action onto the operational volume around the fixed asset |

Read side by side, this looks like the two variables were accidentally swapped in `ForgeEnv` (see #5424). The FORGE implementation is, however, faithful to the FORGE paper:

- The paper defines the action as a relative pose applied to the fixed part's pose to obtain an absolute target, which "is clipped by an action scale, λ, to ensure that the target is not too far from the EE's current pose" (Sec. III-B, Eq. 6), and states "we allow targets to be up to 5cm away in all directions" (the operational volume, i.e. `pos_action_bounds = 0.05`).
- λ is listed in the paper's dynamics randomization table (Appendix A) as "Action Scale: λ ∈ [1.6, 2.5] cm". With the implementation's noise scheme (`x * m` or `x / m` with `m = 1 + U(0,1) · noise_level`), `pos_action_threshold = 0.02` and `pos_threshold_noise_level = 0.25` give exactly `0.02 × [1/1.25, 1.25] = [1.6, 2.5] cm`. The same check works for the controller gains: `565 × [1/1.41, 1.41] ≈ [400, 800]`, matching the paper's "Controller Gains [400, 800]".
- Since FORGE actions are positions (not displacements), the per-step motion limit can only be realized as a clip on the delta to the current EE pose — a multiplicative scale on the action cannot play that role in this action space.

Because this keeps being read as a bug, this PR documents both semantics where a reader would look for them: a class docstring on `CtrlCfg` (Factory semantics), a class docstring on `ForgeCtrlCfg` (FORGE semantics, the λ correspondence and the randomization ranges), and an expanded `ForgeEnv._apply_action` docstring with the paper reference.

Documentation-only change; no behavior is modified.

Related to #5424 (a detailed analysis is posted on the issue).

items.title: [Proposal] Improvements to support distribution and third-party packaging
items.body:
### Proposal

I'm attempting to package IsaacLab 3.0 as a native conda-forge package, similar to what I recently did with newton:
- https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/discussions/2130

While working on this, I identified several issues that currently require hacks or patches during third-party packaging. It would be very helpful to address them directly upstream:

1. Automatically discover subpackages by modifying the following:
   https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/fc6746cae55710c0a375d50775fe55a5a922bff6/source/isaaclab/setup.py#L137
   with:
   ```py
   packages=find_packages(include=["isaaclab*"]),
   ```
   Without this modifications, `pip` would install only the top-level package.
1. With automatic discovery, there is a missing `isaaclab/ui/__init__.py` file to mark it as package.
1. Include as `package_data` all the resources used by the Python package like the [`extension.toml`](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/fc6746cae55710c0a375d50775fe55a5a922bff6/source/isaaclab/isaaclab/__init__.py#L19) files and modify the hardcoded path such that it works both in normal and editable installations.
1.  The `toml` dependency used to read those files is missing in most of the packages. If the wheel is missing in some of the Python versions, you can use the [environment markers](https://peps.python.org/pep-0508/#environment-markers).
1. Move the [testing dependencies](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/fc6746cae55710c0a375d50775fe55a5a922bff6/source/isaaclab/setup.py#L47-L56) to a new extra (or uv group if you are switching to uv).

Beyond these fixes, there are also some structural improvements worth considering:

1. IsaacLab currently pins most dependencies to exact patch versions. This is usually not recommended in Python because it overconstrains the environment and can prevent installation alongside other packages with different requirements. A more common approach is to use `>=` with a minimum supported version, or [`~=`](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/#compatible-release) for a more conservative constraint that still allows compatible updates. In practice, reproducibility is typically handled through `requirements.txt` (legacy) or lock files (for tools like uv or pixi). For this reason, it would be beneficial to relax the current version pinning.
2. Python packaging tooling has improved significantly in recent years. Some improvements worth considering for the 3.0 refactor:
   - Switch to `uv` as the default package manager.
   - Use [`hatch`](https://github.com/pypa/hatch) instead of `setuptools`.
   - Move package configuration from the legacy `setup.py` to `pyproject.toml`.

### Motivation

There are a few packaging details in IsaacLab 3.0 that prevent clean third-party packaging. Fixing these issues would remove the need to patch the project before packaging and improve compliance with modern Python packaging standards.

### Alternatives

N/A.

### Build Info

This issue mainly targets the upcoming 3.0 release ([develop](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/tree/develop) branch), but it also applies to previous versions.

Due to the limitations in redistributing IsaacSim, I'm currently focusing on streamlining all components needed for a kitless installation, as documented here:
- https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/develop/source/setup/installation/kitless_installation.html

This effort could also help validate that the kitless installation works correctly in environments different from the ones used by the development team, improving the general usability of the project.

Additionally, to support this goal, there is a set of dependencies currently downloaded from the Nvidia Python Index. Is it possible to redistribute them through third-party channels? If not, would it be possible to make them optional dependencies?

https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/fc6746cae55710c0a375d50775fe55a5a922bff6/source/isaaclab/setup.py#L46

https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/fc6746cae55710c0a375d50775fe55a5a922bff6/source/isaaclab_mimic/setup.py#L31

Regarding `nvidia-srl-usd-to-urdf`, it seems [available on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/nvidia-srl-usd-to-urdf/) as a pure-Python wheel, but the gitlab sources have disappeared.

### Additional context

Refer to the following PR where I'm trying to package the project as a native conda-forge recipe:

items.title: Add the perf-smoke performance regression gate
items.body:
Adds a performance regression gate for pull requests. It benchmarks a fixed matrix of tasks on the L40S runner pool, compares each result against a rolling baseline stored on the `perf-baselines` branch, and posts a per-task verdict as a sticky PR comment and per-task commit statuses.

The gate is advisory. `gate_config.json` sets `blocking: false`, so it never fails a PR on its own. Making it an enforcing required check would be a separate rollout.

## How a run works

`perf-smoke-test.yaml` runs six jobs.

`config` reads the Isaac Sim version from `config.yaml`, and `validate` runs static checks on `tasks.json` so a malformed matrix fails on a free runner in seconds rather than after an hour of GPU time. Both are skipped for draft PRs.

`bench` fans out one GPU job per task/backend bucket. Each job resolves and pulls the CI image, restores a Warp JIT cache keyed on the Warp version, runs `perf_runtime.py` inside Docker with the repo bind-mounted, retries once on failure, normalizes the output into `perf_smoke_test_result.json`, and posts a per-task commit status.

`aggregate` downloads every bench artifact, loads the matching baselines, runs the oracle, writes the summary comment, and uploads results to omni-github. It runs with `always()` so a crashed bucket still gets reported instead of vanishing.

`baseline_update` appends the run's samples to `perf-baselines`, and only on pushes to `main`, `develop`, or a release branch. Pull requests are strictly read-only against the baseline branch, so nothing a PR does can move the numbers it is judged against.

`reseed` fills buckets that came out under-filled, by calling the seeding workflow for just those tasks at the pushed commit. Without it, a bucket that resets (say, after a launch-config change) would take five separate pushes to become useful again. It is self-limiting: once a bucket is full it stops being reported as under-filled, and seeding writes to `perf-baselines`, which triggers no workflow.

## How the verdict is decided

`oracle.py` produces one of `PASS`, `WARN`, `BLOCK`, or `HARD_FAILURE` per bucket, and the most severe signal wins.

A run is a `HARD_FAILURE` if the launch configuration did not match what was requested, if the result file is missing, or if the reported FPS is missing or not positive. A run reporting no forward progress is a dead run rather than a slow one, so it fails regardless of what the baseline says.

Otherwise the result is compared against the rolling window. The baseline contributes a median and a median absolute deviation, and the gate blocks when the measured FPS falls below `median - 4.0 x MAD` **and** the drop is at least 3 percent. The percentage floor exists so that a bucket with an unusually tight MAD cannot block on a fraction of a percent. Between `median - 2.5 x MAD` and the block line the verdict is `WARN`. There is also a noise floor so that a very tight baseline does not make the thresholds hypersensitive.

Buckets can additionally declare fixed FPS floors in `tasks.json`. A crossed gating floor forces a `BLOCK` on its own; a reporting-only floor is recorded without changing the verdict.

With no baseline, or fewer than five samples in the window, the verdict is `WARN` and the reason is stated as `NO_BASELINE` or `INSUFFICIENT_WINDOW`. The gate says it does not know rather than implying a pass.

## What gets measured

Nine task/backend buckets:

- `Isaac-Cartpole-Direct` on physx and on newton
- `Isaac-Velocity-Flat-G1` on physx and on newton
- `IsaacContrib-Factory-GearMesh-Direct` on physx
- `Isaac-Reorient-Cube-Shadow-Camera-Benchmark-Direct` across four physics/renderer combinations (physx and newton, each with the RTX renderer and the Newton renderer)

`perf_runtime.py` drives each task with random actions and no policy, discards warmup frames at the source, and reports steady-state mean FPS.

## Baselines and how samples are matched

Baselines live on the orphan `perf-baselines` branch as append-only NDJSON, one file per GPU model, task, and backend.

A stored sample is only eligible if it matches on GPU model, task, backend, target branch, launch-config hash, baseline epoch, benchmark contract hash, and runtime contract hash, and if its commit is an ancestor of the PR's merge base. Ancestry matters because a sample from an unmerged branch describes code that may never land. The window holds between 5 and 20 samples, nearest commits first.

The hashes are the reason a verdict can be trusted: change the number of environments, the seed, the frame count, or the CUDA/driver pairing, and the fingerprint changes, so old samples stop matching instead of being silently compared against a different experiment.

## Keeping the environment stable

`image_era.py` derives a key from the container's inputs and looks it up in a manifest on `perf-baselines`. When an immutable image is recorded for that key the gate pins it; otherwise it falls back to the published `latest-develop` tag, and builds only if that pull fails. Pinning matters because a nightly rebuild of a floating tag would otherwise shift the environment underneath a baseline that was measured in the old one.

## When something goes wrong

Benchmarks retry once, since a single flaky container start should not read as a regression.

A crash always exits non-zero. Advisory mode suppresses regression failures, not execution failures, so a benchmark that never ran cannot be mistaken for one that ran fine.

Skew detection in `aggregate.py` handles one specific case that would otherwise blame the wrong person. The gate mounts PR source over a prebuilt image, so between a dependency pin landing and the next image publish, source can reference a symbol the installed package does not have yet. When a crash log shows a missing name from a package the image provides (`newton`, `warp`, `isaacsim`, `mujoco`, and so on), the summary reports a stale CI image and those tasks stay advisory. Isaac Lab's own source is mounted from the PR, so a missing symbol there is a real defect and still fails.

## Workflows

`perf-smoke-test.yaml` is the gate itself, described above.

`perf-smoke-seed-baselines.yaml` walks a slice of a branch's history, re-runs each commit's own benchmark, and appends the results, so a new bucket can be filled without waiting for five organic pushes. It runs on manual dispatch, defaulting to a dry run, and is called by the gate's reseed job. It resolves its image through the same code path the gate uses, so seeded samples and live runs share an environment.

`perf-smoke-unit-tests.yaml` runs the gate's own tests on `ubuntu-latest`.

## The Python

Under `tools/perf_smoke_test/`, roughly by role:

- Deciding: `oracle.py`, `gate_types.py`, `gate_config.py`
- Baselines: `baseline_manager.py`, `verify_baselines.py`, `seed_baselines.py`
- Identity and reproducibility: `backend_identity.py`, `gpu_identity.py`, `launch_config.py`, `runtime_contract.py`, `contracts.py`, `hashing.py`, `image_era.py`
- Running and normalizing: `perf_runtime.py`, `build_bench_result.py`, `benchmark_result_adapter.py`, `write_launch_config.py`
- Matrix and config: `tasks.json`, `task_config.py`, `tasks_to_ci_matrix.py`, `validate_tasks.py`, `gate_config.json`
- Reporting: `aggregate.py`, `omni_github.py`, `github_gate_context.py`

`tools/subprocess_runner.py` classifies which phase a failed subprocess died in, which is what lets a config mismatch be told apart from a crash mid-benchmark.

## Tests

72 tests covering the oracle's verdicts and thresholds, baseline matching and ancestry, contract hashing, seeding and cache isolation, skew detection, and the aggregate reporting path.

They are pure Python: no GPU, no simulator, no Isaac Lab install. `tools/perf_smoke_test/pyproject.toml` makes pytest root there so the isaaclab-importing `tools/conftest.py` above it is not loaded, which is the same arrangement `tools/skills/` and `tools/changelog/` already use.

## What to know before merging

It runs on every PR into develop from day one. The trigger list already covers `pull_request: [main, develop, release/**]`, so that is real L40S pool time on every PR. More of a capacity question than a code question.

Baselines start empty. Every sample on `perf-baselines` today is stamped `target_branch: perf-smoke/develop-staging`, and matching requires an exact target-branch match, so none carry over. All nine buckets begin with no baseline and report `NO_BASELINE` or `INSUFFICIENT_WINDOW` until five samples accumulate, which happens on its own from `develop` pushes. It sorts itself out after a few, but the gate is not useful on day one.

Six of the nine buckets have inert thresholds. Every Newton bucket and three camera buckets carry a `0.0` hard floor, which can never fire. Harmless while the gate is advisory, but they need real values before it could block anything.

There is no runner-stability verdict yet. The PhysX buckets produced clean samples on July 28; the Newton buckets never ran, because the staging branch had drifted 216 commits behind and its source called `newton.solvers.SolverNotifyFlags`, renamed to `ModelFlags` in the meantime. That was the frozen branch showing its age rather than a problem with the gate, and it does not arise on `develop`, where source and image move together. Landing here rather than on staging is what retires that failure mode. This supersedes #6863, which carried the same fixes against staging.

## Test plan

- [x] 72 passed, 1 skipped via `python3 -m pytest tools/perf_smoke_test/`
- [x] Tests collect and pass with no Isaac Lab install and no pytest flags
- [x] All pre-commit hooks pass

- [x] No changelog fragment required; the check only demands one for packages touched under `source/`
- [ ] After merge: first `develop` push runs the gate and begins filling baselines
- [ ] Confirm no image build or seeding run is triggered unprompted

items.title: Order PhysX-convention siblings by authored joint order on Newton
items.body:
# Description

`joint_ordering="physx"` / `body_ordering="physx"` on a non-PhysX backend is resolved from a temporary Newton import
that uses `joint_ordering="bfs"`. PhysX lists links breadth-first too, but it orders the children of a link by the
authored order of their joint prims. Newton orders them by the UsdPhysics parse result, which is sorted by prim path.
Whenever siblings are not authored alphabetically, the resolved order is silently permuted. This affects the Shadow
Hand, Digit and Humanoid assets.

The fix keeps the Newton prototype view for topology and naming and walks its joints breadth-first again, with the
child joints of each link in the stage-traversal order of their joint prims. The change is limited to
`ordering_resolvers.py`.

The resolver runs once when the articulation is initialized, and its result is cached. It adds one prim traversal of
the source asset and adds nothing to the per-step path.

Fixes #8225

A simulator-free unit test traverses a two-finger tree whose sibling joints are authored in reverse path order and
checks the PhysX sibling order. It fails with the sibling sort removed (the path-sorted order comes back) and passes
with this change.

Results on the official assets, comparing live PhysX with Newton + `"physx"`:
- Shadow: before 12/24 joints misplaced, after 0.
- Digit: before 37/50 joints misplaced, after 0.
- Humanoid: before 21/21 joints misplaced, after 0 (compared without the `:<axis>` DoF suffix, which already differs
  between the backends).
- Go2, G1, H1, ANYmal-D, Franka, Spot, Allegro, KUKA-Allegro, GR1-T2, UR10, Cartpole: 0 before and 0 after.

With an ordering set, UR10e + Robotiq 2F-85 fails on Newton because of duplicate `base_link` body names, which is
unrelated; its resolved `"physx"` joint order equals live PhysX before and after.

items.title: [Question]  Inconsistent and potentially swapped usage of pos_action_bounds and pos_action_threshold between FactoryEnv and ForgeEnv
items.body:
### Question While studying the source code for the `direct/factory` and `direct/forge` environments, I noticed a significant discrepancy in how p`os_action_bounds` and `pos_action_threshold` (and their rotational counterparts) are applied to the policy actions. It seems these two variables might have been accidentally swapped in `forge_env.py`. 1. The Discrepancy in Action Scaling vs. Clipping in [FactoryEnv](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/main/source/isaaclab_tasks/isaaclab_tasks/direct/factory/factory_env.py) `_apply_action()`: - `pos_threshold`is used as the **action scale**:`pos_actions = self.actions[:, 0:3] * self.pos_threshold` - `pos_action_bounds` is used to clip the maximum workspace range:`torch.clip(delta_pos, -self.cfg.ctrl.pos_action_bounds[0], ...)` in [ForgeEnv](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/main/source/isaaclab_tasks/isaaclab_tasks/direct/forge/forge_env.py) `_apply_action()`: - `pos_action_bounds`is used as the **action scale**:`pos_actions = pos_actions @ torch.diag(torch.tensor(self.cfg.ctrl.pos_action_bounds, ...)) - `pos_threshold` is used to clip the delta step:`torch.clip(self.delta_pos, -self.pos_threshold, self.pos_threshold)`
2. The Contradiction with Config Values:in [FactoryEnvCfg](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/blob/main/source/isaaclab_tasks/isaaclab_tasks/direct/factory/factory_env_cfg.py) `CtrlCfg`,the default definitions are: - `pos_action_bounds = [0.05, 0.05, 0.05]` - `pos_action_threshold = [0.02, 0.02, 0.02]` Since `bounds `is much larger than `threshold`, the naming implies `bounds` should be the absolute safety limit, while `threshold `is the maximum single-step increment. The way they are used in `ForgeEnv` contradicts this intuition. 3. The Domain Randomization Paradox in `ForgeEnv`: in `ForgeEnv._reset_idx()`, domain randomization (noise) is added to `self.pos_threshold` ``` self.pos_threshold = forge_utils.get_random_prop_gains( self.pos_threshold, self.cfg.ctrl.pos_threshold_noise_level, ... ) ``` If `pos_threshold` is simply a hard clipping limit (as currently used in `Forge_Env`'s clipping), applying noise to it seems physically meaningless. However, if `pos_threshold` was originally intended to be the action scale (as it is in `FactoryEnv`), then adding noise makes perfect sense. ### Questions: 1. Was the swapping of these two variables in `ForgeEnv` intentional, or is it a bug? 2. If intentional, could you clarify the physical meaning of randomizing the clipping limit *`pos_threshold` in Forge)? Thank you for your time and for maintaining this great repository! ### Build Info - Isaac Lab Version: 2.2.1 - Isaac Sim Version: [4.5]

items.title: [Proposal] Avoid sudo commands in Pip recommended installation
items.body:
### Proposal

When using IsaacLab/Sim in shared machines, most of the times one does not have **sudo** permissions.
Therefore, the **Pip recommended installation** should avoid to use any **sudo** command, such as:

1. `sudo apt install cmake build-essential`
2. or the ones executed by `./isaaclab.sh`

### Motivation
Allow **Pip recommended installation** of IsaacLab/Sim in shared machines without **sudo** permissions.
